newItems.proposedInterface: For arbitrary smooth maps of Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds and WF(u) disjoint N_f, construct the canonical pullback with the full standard WF upper bound. Prove cutoff and coordinate independence, local restriction compatibility, overlap agreement and gluing. Locally prove sequential continuity for the explicitly defined controlled convergence (weak distribution convergence, common finite-order bound and uniform rapid localized Fourier bounds on every closed regular cone). This is enough for canonical regularization limits and is not an unsupported claim of full joint continuity in a named microlocal topology.
proofConstruction: Choose a compact nonnegative test cutoff equal to1 on a unit ball, normalize its positive finite Lebesgue integral, and form rho_epsilon. Positivity can be verified by an interior box; only existing box-volume facts are needed. For compactly localized u, u_epsilon=rho_epsilon*u is smooth by the exact smooth-parameter pairing supplier. Prove test convergence by the finite-order estimate and convergence of the translated test average in each fixed-support derivative seminorm. Fourier transform is rhohat(epsilon eta) uhat(eta), giving uniform polynomial bounds and uniform rapid bounds on regular cones. Cutoff convolution estimates from chart-invariance3.2 transfer these bounds to all smaller localizations. No unavailable general distribution-mollifier theorem is assumed.

Fix x0 first. Choose one N chart about x0 and one M chart about f(x0), then shrink both. The unit conormal kernel of df_x0^T is compact and disjoint from the fiber WF(u). Closedness and the compact unit sphere give a small target base patch and a cone V about those normal directions disjoint from every localized singular direction there. Shrink the source patch so |df_x^T eta|>=c|eta| outside V, uniformly. If the normal set is empty use V empty. This is a local compact separation argument, not a global cone over f(supp omega).

On one such patch define the absolutely convergent Fourier pairing using T_omega(eta)=integral exp(2pi i f(x).eta)omega(x). In V, uhat has arbitrary decay; off V, repeated integration by parts in x has uniform phase-gradient lower bound. Show the adjoint differential operators after N iterations have amplitude coefficients bounded by C_N |eta|^(-N), including all compact support derivatives of omega through a finite order. Choose N above the finite-order growth and frequency dimension. This proves distribution continuity and controlled-sequence continuity by dominated convergence.

Prove the full output WF estimate with phase f(x).eta-x.xi. Outside the desired cotangent image, shrink the base and direction cones. In the regular eta region with |eta| comparable to or greater than |xi| use rapid input decay; in |eta| small relative to |xi| use phase nonstationarity. In the singular eta region transversality and exclusion of the output cone give |df_x^T eta-xi|>=c(|eta|+|xi|). Integrate the repeated-by-parts bound above the required polynomial growth and frequency dimension. Track the same estimates uniformly for controlled regularizations.

If two target cutoffs agree near f(supp omega), their difference w vanishes on such a neighborhood. Its compact mollifications vanish at f(supp omega) for all sufficiently small epsilon. Controlled-sequence continuity then makes the candidate pullback of w zero. Thus target cutoff independence and locality follow, with compactly supported mollifiers essential to this support argument.

Existing chart-change phase estimates, repeated uniformly with the same common finite-order/cone bounds, transport controlled convergence between target charts. Transform the same smooth regularizing sequence rather than choosing unrelated sequences. For each smooth approximant, the two candidate pairings agree by the ordinary scalar/density change-of-variables formula. Dominated limits prove target chart covariance. The same argument for domain coordinate changes uses the actual test-density Jacobian. This proves overlap agreement with the intrinsic diffeomorphism pullback already defined locally.

For each compact test support choose finitely many small source patches of the preceding kind. Construct a finite smooth partition equal to1 near that support by cutoffs and division by their positive sum. Sum the local pairings. A double-partition refinement plus overlap agreement proves independence. Each fixed-support seminorm bound is a finite sum, so the test-density inductive-limit definition gives a global distribution. Empty domains and zero-dimensional charts are treated separately; in dimension0 all local distributions are scalar functions and the same construction is just ordinary pullback. Nonproper f causes no problem because only compact test supports and their compact images enter.

newItems.proposedInterface: For the compact polynomial coefficient kernels of two original microcausal functionals, every finite labelled matching with singular Hadamard W edges only from the first coefficient block to the second, and arbitrary smooth K self-edges or cross edges, has a canonical simultaneous contraction. Every ordering of its finite products and compact coordinate integrations gives that same result, with the usual external derivative/permutation formulas. This is precisely the Wick-change matching class; it does not assert arbitrary singular self-contractions Gamma_W exist.
proofConstruction: First prove the local finite-family product lemma: if closed cones Gamma_j have no nonzero simultaneous zero sum (zero entries allowed), then on a sufficiently small compact base patch the unit total-frequency tuple has a positive lower bound for |sum eta_j| whenever all frequencies lie in their cones. A frequency tuple either has a comparable-size frequency in a regular cone or has |sum eta_j| comparable to total size. The multi-frequency formula prod uhat_j(eta_j) phihat(-sum eta_j) is therefore absolutely integrable after taking rapid-decay powers above all finite-order bounds and the total integration dimension. Give the explicit finite decomposition and integrable majorant; do not infer this from pairwise transversality alone.

Use controlled smooth regularizations of all factors with independent epsilon parameters. The same conic estimates give a common integrable majorant, so the limit is independent of the smoothing path and equals every iterated product whenever its intermediate conormal conditions hold. The modulated-test version tracks uniform intermediate WF bounds. Smooth factors and coordinate changes are covered by the first helper; local products therefore agree across cutoffs/charts.

For the actual two-original-vertex matching, prove the full and every partial conormal condition from microcausality. A zero total covector forces contracted entries of the first block to be past null or zero and of the second block future null or zero; remaining entries are zero. Any nonzero edge makes both affected block tuples nonzero and forbidden. Smooth K edges add no singular directions. Include the cases where one coefficient covector is zero, a contraction count is0, or only smooth edges occur.

When some matched variables are already integrated out, a possible obstruction for a remaining product lifts by the projection WF estimate with zero covectors in all previously integrated slots. The same full-block future/past contradiction still excludes it. Thus all intermediate matching operations actually used by the exponential/binomial expansion are admissible; no unverified admissibility hypothesis is left to the caller.

With fixed compact coefficient supports, choose cutoffs on their compact slot projections; every full and intermediate product has one common compact support. Prove projection formula and Fubini compatibility of compact pushforwards by the same jointly regularized smooth expression. Its ordinary iterated integrals agree, and the common Fourier majorants give equality in all limits. Integration against noncompact smooth K or the metric density is harmless after these explicit support cutoffs. Handle free external slots by arbitrary compact test densities and integrate the matched slots only.

Prove symmetry under slot relabeling and the derivative Leibniz rule directly on the finite coefficient kernels. All contractions remove distinct labelled original slots, so repeated operations are exactly matchings. This permits the Wick finite exponential rearrangement without invoking smooth-coefficient density in the wrong topology or singular Gamma_W.
